newsitem.title: UK: Halt Indonesia arms exports - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Halt Indonesia arms exports - Amnesty.

text.p: Amnesty International on Monday urged Britain to stop exporting machineguns, armoured personnel vehicles and computer surveillance systems to Indonesia.

"The almost complete lack of accountability and human rights training of security forces in Indonesia means that military equipment supplied to Indonesia's Armed Forces (ABRI) always has the potential to be deployed in operations during which human rights violations are committed," it said.
The human rights pressure group said the issue provided Britain's new Labour government a perfect opportunity to prove its commitment to place human rights at the heart of foreign policy.

Amnesty International's British director David Bull said: "ABRI is focused primarily on combating internal dissent rather than external threats and its role is to monitor and suppress dissent throughout Indonesia and East Timor.
"It has committed unlawful killings, disappearances, torture and arbitrary arrest."
He said Amnesty had also called for the sale of water cannon to be suspended pending investigations by the British government.
